synthesis.indonesia: 230 Indonesia, SEA, or APAC research records are indexed across economics, equities, strategy, credit, private markets, and thematic research.
synthesis.global: 305 verified research records from 61 publishers are searchable; 284 expose an open or direct-download route.

research.provenance_note: Research records are source-linked metadata. Cockpit does not reproduce full reports or treat broker opinions as facts.

core.label: Real GDP Growth
core.commentary: Annual growth is firm, but the quarter contracted and government consumption was a major driver.

core.label: PMI-BI Manufacturing
core.commentary: Manufacturing remains above the 50 expansion threshold; the next-quarter expectation is stronger.

core.label: Consumer Confidence
core.commentary: Consumers remain optimistic, but the level alone does not establish improvement from May.

core.label: Retail Sales Index
core.commentary: The expected index remains high, but the monthly contraction points to softer near-term spending.

core.label: Headline CPI Inflation
core.commentary: Headline inflation accelerated and is close to the upper edge of Bank Indonesia's target corridor.

core.label: Core Inflation
core.commentary: Core inflation rose but remains inside the policy target corridor, indicating contained underlying pressure.

core.label: Volatile Food Inflation
core.commentary: Food inflation eased from May, although its level remains high enough to pressure household purchasing power.

core.label: Administered-Price Inflation
core.commentary: Regulated-price inflation accelerated sharply as non-subsidised fuel and airfares increased.

core.label: BI Policy Rate
core.commentary: The higher policy setting supports rupiah stability while raising domestic funding and valuation hurdles.

core.label: FX Reserves
core.commentary: Reserve cover remains adequate; the key watch is whether rupiah defence causes persistent drawdowns.

core.label: Trade Balance
core.commentary: The monthly deficit weakens near-term FX support even though the year-to-date balance remains positive.

core.label: Current Account
core.commentary: The deficit is manageable but increases dependence on direct and portfolio investment inflows.

core.label: APBN Deficit
core.commentary: The first-half deficit is contained, while the full-year outlook is close enough to the legal ceiling to monitor.

core.label: Credit Growth / Gross NPL
core.commentary: Lending is expanding while headline asset quality remains contained.

detail.label: Business Activity Survey
detail.commentary: The higher weighted net balance indicates broader business expansion.

detail.label: Wholesale Price Inflation
detail.commentary: Upstream price pressure is elevated and may pass through to producer margins and consumer prices.

detail.label: External Debt
detail.commentary: Currency mix and near-term refinancing needs matter more than the headline stock.

detail.label: Revenue / Spending
detail.commentary: Revenue quality and productive spending composition determine the growth impact.

detail.label: Unemployment / Average Wage
detail.commentary: Unemployment improved, while real wage growth and formal-job quality remain the key checks.

detail.label: Net NPL / Loan at Risk
detail.commentary: Both arrears and broader restructured exposures should stay contained as credit expands.

detail.label: CAR / LCR
detail.commentary: Capital and liquidity buffers remain comfortably above regulatory minimums.

ratings.label: S&P Global
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains investment grade. S&P expects the recent weakening in fiscal and external indicators to be temporary.

ratings.label: Fitch Ratings
ratings.commentary: The rating remains investment grade, but the negative outlook flags policy-consistency, fiscal, and external-buffer risks.

ratings.label: Moody's
ratings.commentary: Moody's kept Indonesia one notch above its investment-grade floor while highlighting lower policy predictability.

ratings.label: MSCI Indonesia
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains in MSCI's emerging-market universe, while shareholder transparency and coordinated-trading concerns remain under review.

ratings.label: FTSE Russell
ratings.commentary: FTSE Russell kept Indonesia at Secondary Emerging while monitoring transparency, free-float, governance, and market-integrity reforms.

country_risk.label: Rupiah 1M Move
country_risk.commentary: A positive USD/IDR move means rupiah depreciation; persistent weakening raises imported-inflation and foreign-flow risk.

country_risk.label: USD/IDR Realized Volatility
country_risk.commentary: Annualized daily volatility measures rupiah instability; it complements, but does not replace, sovereign-spread data.

country_risk.label: JCI Realized Volatility
country_risk.commentary: Annualized JCI volatility tracks market stress and position-sizing risk rather than fundamental value.

country_risk.label: JCI 6M Max Drawdown
country_risk.commentary: Peak-to-trough loss shows realized equity stress within the available six-month history.

macro_indicators.refresh_policy: Markets refresh every 30 minutes. Official macro cards advance only after a newer release is source-checked; release periods are shown on every card.
macro_indicators.methodology_note: Direction compares only published periods or stated benchmarks. Green means improving, red means deteriorating, and grey means stable, mixed, or insufficient trend evidence.
macro_indicators.country_risk_note: Market-priced risk measures use transparent 30-minute telemetry and daily price history. The ID-US yield differential is a carry/funding proxy, not CDS or JPM EMBI. Proprietary sovereign spreads and unavailable flow data are omitted rather than estimated.

podcasts.title: Kenapa “Tokoh Penting” Diburu Aparat? - Ft. Tom Lembong
podcasts.thesis: New The Overpost episode — open to listen.

podcasts.title: Our Smaller Model Beat Opus on Finance Tasks - Alexander Shevchenko, Ramp
podcasts.thesis: Alexander Shevchenko of Ramp Labs explains why an application company still runs applied research instead of waiting for the next frontier model.

podcasts.title: AI Labs Will Trap You or Replace You - Dillon Rolnick, Nous Research
podcasts.thesis: Dillon Rolnick, CEO of Nous Research, argues that as AI models commoditize, the labs that spent trillions building them have two ways to earn it back: lock businesses into their platforms and raise prices, or point their own systems at lucrative industries like finance and compete directly.

podcasts.title: Robots Will Be Trained on Video Games - Pim de Witte, General Intuition
podcasts.thesis: Pim de Witte of General Intuition, the team behind the Medal game recorder, argues that models built to act in space and time need a different design than LLMs, which work turn by turn. His models take in frames and send out actions continuously, the way a gamer plays.

podcasts.title: Trump Just Lost the Midterms... Now What?
podcasts.thesis: What happens if Donald Trump loses the 2026 midterm elections? A Democratic takeover of the House or Senate could reshape Trump's economic agenda, U.S. fiscal policy, and the stock market outlook for 2027.

podcasts.title: The Closest Thing We Have to Alien Matter
podcasts.thesis: If you backed us on Kickstarter, don’t worry, your game will ship before any pre-orders are fulfilled. ▀▀▀ ▀▀▀ A massive thank you to Prof. Martin Zwierlein for his enthusiasm and helping us get the specifics of superfluidity and BECs right.

podcasts.title: The New AI Agents That Shop, Plan, and Gossip
podcasts.thesis: Will we have one AI assistant that does everything, or an entire network of agents that know different parts of our lives? David Pawlan, creator of Assistant Benchmark, returns with Anish Acharya and Josh Elman to take stock of how quickly the agent landscape has changed.

podcasts.title: 10 Habits PhDs Must Unlearn To Build a Startup | Startup School
podcasts.thesis: Google, Anthropic, and Databricks were all started by founders with PhDs. But they’re the exceptions. Most academic founders fail, because the instincts that get you published are the ones that can get you killed in a startup. Francois Chaubard knows both sides.

podcasts.title: What Happens When the AI Boom Slows Down
podcasts.thesis: Martin Casado, General Partner at Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), joins Patrick to explore why AI represents an industrial revolution rather than another software cycle.

podcasts.title: Don't Approve the AI Model. Approve the App - Doneyli De Jesus, Langfuse
podcasts.thesis: Doneyli De Jesus, who leads AI engineering solutions at Langfuse by ClickHouse, shares how his team helped a top-five bank put deployment gates on AI agents. Banks don't certify models, they certify applications, and they need setups that are on-premises, gated and air-gapped.

podcasts.title: Did the Knicks’ phishing test go too far? Plus, hackers pose as IT in Teams
podcasts.thesis: Click to claim your free Knicks championship ring, and you might end up in security training. First, MSG sends staff an offer to pick their own championship ring, and everyone who clicks lands in mandatory security training.

podcasts.title: Why Datasite Stopped Building Its Own Parsing - Adit Abraham, Reducto & Raj Bakhru, Datasite
podcasts.thesis: Datasite global CTO Raj Bakhru talks with Reducto co-founder and CEO Adit Abraham about leading AI at a platform that handles about 60% of deals over $100 million.

podcasts.title: Building the AI Agent Is Easy. Proving It's Safe Isn't - Jonathan Osborne, NatWest
podcasts.thesis: NatWest lead AI engineer Jonathan Osborne shares how the UK's second-largest retail bank, with 19 million customers and about 100,000 assistant conversations a day, is moving its digital assistant Cora from scripted answers to AI agents.

podcasts.title: Redis CEO: AI Agents Need Context, Not Raw Intelligence
podcasts.thesis: Moving AI agents from pilot to production depends less on model intelligence than on the business context and data the agents are given.

podcasts.title: All-In Podcast REACTS to Democrat Sweep!
podcasts.thesis: Show Notes: Follow the besties: Follow on X: Follow on Instagram: Follow on TikTok: Follow on LinkedIn: Intro Music Credit: Intro Video Credit: #allin #tech #news

podcasts.title: Truth, Not Hype: How CIOs Can Survive AI Vendors
podcasts.thesis: AI vendors price their products in credits and units that no two products measure the same way, and buyers often pay for more than they understand.

podcasts.title: Cisco's President: "Agentic AI Will Write Our Code"
podcasts.thesis: Agentic AI transformation means rethinking every workflow through the lens of AI agents.

podcasts.title: IHSG, Rupiah 18.000 & Kenapa 2027 Bakal Lebih BERAT? - Ft. Tom Lembong
podcasts.thesis: Menuju tahun 2027, Indonesia diprediksi masuk ke fase ekonomi terberat bukan hanya karena ancaman MSCI tapi juga karena ancaman geopolitik.

podcasts.title: Andrew Huberman on Focus, Energy, and Performing at Your Best
podcasts.thesis: If you could do only three things for your health, what should they be? Andrew Huberman’s answer is surprisingly straightforward: get bright light shortly after waking, resistance train, and make the sleep you can get as high-quality as possible.

podcasts.title: How Korea built a world class defence industry from scratch
podcasts.thesis: WANT AN IN-DEPTH INDUSTRIAL POLICY MASTERCLASS? LIKE CHATTING ECON WITH ME? △ I have a private Discord server for Senior and Chief economist Patrons / members. SOURCES: I've linked my sources in the blog that goes along with this video.

podcasts.title: From AI Infrastructure to the 6G Future
podcasts.thesis: In this Telecom Special Address from NVIDIA GTC Berlin, Ronnie Vasishta, SVP of Telecom at NVIDIA, explores how AI-RAN, accelerated computing, and AI inference at the edge are shaping the path to 6G.

podcasts.title: Can Your AI Use Sensitive Data Safely? 5 Capabilities You Need
podcasts.thesis: Sensitive data makes AI powerful, but also risky. Jeff Crume explains five essential capabilities for using sensitive data safely across AI systems, agents, tools, and RAG pipelines.
